Bell had one deep target and zero red zone targets. We'll see if his role continues to grow this week, but he's an interesting flex play. Minnesota has allowed the 11th-most yards per target and the tenth-most fantasy points per opportunity to perimeter wide receivers.
Mike Evans sustained a rib injury last week. He opened this week with a DNP. I'll update his outlook on Friday.
Adonai Mitchell is still working through a finger injury. He opened this week with a DNP. I'm expecting him to be out again this week.
Caleb Douglas opened this week with a DNP (ankle). I'm expecting him to miss Week 4, but I'll update his outlook on Friday.

Tyler Warren is humming along as the TE8 in fantasy points per game. Warren has a 22.4% target share and 19.2% first-read share, while his per-route efficiency hasn't been great. He has only 1.00 YPRR, 4.39 yards after the catch per reception, and 0.045 first downs per route run. None of those metrics are good, but we know the type of talent Warren has, so I'm not pressing any panic button after only three games when his quarterback has been playing horrible football. Warren has three red zone targets and zero deep targets. Warren should have a nice week against a Washington pass defense that has allowed the third-most yards per target and the most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Juwan Johnson was an amazing late-round selection this summer. He has been producing as the TE4 in fantasy points per game. Johnson has a 13.6% target share, 1.73 YPRR, SIX red zone targets, a deep target, and a 17.2% first-read share. Atlanta has held tight ends to the 12th-fewest yards per target, but they have allowed three receiving scores and the eighth-most fantasy points per opportunity. Johnson is a rock-solid TE1.

After his standout performance last week, Harold Fannin Jr. is the TE10 in fantasy points per game. Posting 24.1 PPR points in a three-game sample can falsely inflate your value like that, though. Fannin was held below 11 PPR points in each of the first two games of the season. He has a 21.7% target share, 1.57 YPRR, two red zone targets, one deep target, and a 17.9% first-read share (third on the team). Fannin could stay hot this week against a pass defense that has allowed the eighth-most yards per target and the ninth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Isaiah Likely is in the same boat as Malik Nabers. He's seeing a high-end market share of the Giants' passing attack. Likely just needs league-average quarterback play to turn it into fantasy production. Last week, Likely had an 84.5% snap share, an 84.6% route share, a 22.7% target share, and a 25% first-read share, turning it into 13 receiving yards (0.59 YPRR). Arizona has been ripped apart by tight ends, allowing the fifth-most yards per target and the third-most fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

Tucker Kraft is the TE27 and hasn't had at least double-digit PPR points in any game this season. Over the last two games, he has had a 70.9% route share with a 13.4% target share, 0.67 YPRR, only 5.0 YAC per reception, and an 18.2% first-read share. Kraft has one deep target and one red zone look. Kraft definitely looks like a player rounding into form coming off a major injury. Could this be the breakout week? It's possible with the matchup. Tampa Bay has allowed the 12th-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends this season.

Dalton Schultz is the TE7 in fantasy points per game, but that is entirely fueled by his performance against Cincy, when he looked like Houston's Brock Bowers. In the other two games this season, Schultz hasn't had more than four receptions and 35 receiving yards in either game. Schultz also saw his route share dip to 64.5% last week, which is something I didn't see coming after his massive Week 2 performance with a 74.6% route share. Overall, Schultz has a 20.7% target share, 2.09 YPRR, one red zone target, zero deep targets, and a 21% first-read share. We could see Schultz's role bounce back this week against a defense that has allowed the tenth-most yards per target and the fifth-most fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

Kenyon Sadiq had a breakout week last week and could keep the good times rolling this week. The Bears have surrendered the tenth-most yards per target to tight ends while only facing Darren Waller in a part-time role in Week 1, an underutilized TJ Hockenson, and a part-time Zach Ertz in Week 3. Last week, Sadiq had a 56.8% route share, a 21.6% target share, 105 receiving yards (4.20 YPRR), zero red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 19.2% first-read share. Sadiq was the TE4 for the week. With Mason Taylor likely out again this week, along with Adonai Mitchell, Sadiq should operate as the number two option in the passing attack with TE1 upside.

Mark Andrews is the TE20 in fantasy points per game, but his usage suggests that a correction is coming in his fantasy output. Andrews has a 65.6% route share, a 23.7% target share, 2.07 YPRR, one red zone target, zero deep targets, and a 25.9% first-read share. All of his per-route metrics have been stellar, but he hasn't been getting high-leverage usage, and he has zero touchdowns this season. Among 38 qualifying tight ends, he is TE14 in XFP per route run. Tennessee hasn't really faced a tough tight end yet. Kenyon Sadiq was only a part-time player in Week 1. Dallas Goedert got hurt in Week 2. Last week, Isaiah Likely had Jameis Winston chucking him uncatchable targets. Andrews could post a strong TE1 stat line this week.

Well, Colston Loveland finally got more usage last week, but it wasn't great, as he was the TE26 for the week. This isn't the type of season that I projected for Loveland. I also didn't foresee Kalif Raymond being a massive part of this passing offense, but it is what it is at this point. Last week, Loveland had an 11.8% target share, 31 receiving yards (1.35 YPRR), and a 10.3% first-read share. This is woeful usage for a player with his talent level. The Jets have held tight ends to the 13th-fewest yards per target and the eighth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity. Loveland is a touchdown-dependent fantasy option only right now.

Over the last two games, Darren Waller has been the TE5 and TE17 in weekly scoring. In those games, Waller has had a 55.6% route share, a 13.1% target share, 1.68 YPRR, two red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 12.2% first-read share. Waller could feast this week against a defense that has allowed the sixth-most yards per target and fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends. Detroit has also allowed the most receiving touchdowns (six) to the position.

Brenton Strange is the TE24 in fantasy points per game with a 71.3% route share, a 12.3% target share, 1.16 YPRR, two red zone targets, zero deep targets, and a 12.1% first-read share. Strange is a viable streaming option at tight end this week or a desperation flex in deeper leagues. Cincy hasn't allowed a receiving score to a tight end yet this season, but they have given up the fourth-most yards per target to the position. Strange could be a TE1 this week.

Jake Ferguson is the TE15 in fantasy points per game that is being fueled by his touchdown equity in the Dallas passing attack. Ferguson has three scores in his last two games while not surpassing 43 receiving yards in any game. Ferguson has only a 10.5% target share, 0.97 YPRR, and an 11% first-read share. Ferguson does have four red zone targets, though. He's essentially a touchdown-or-bust tight end option weekly. Houston has allowed the second-most yards per target to tight ends, but they also rank 16th in fantasy points per opportunity and have allowed zero receiving scores. Ferguson could be a TE1 this week, but he's a risky play.

Since Week 2, Hunter Henry has faded into the background of the Pats' passing attack with an 11.3% target share, 1.02 YPRR, one red zone target, one deep target, and a 14.7% first-read share. Henry has averaged 4.2 fantasy points per game. I don't see any of this changing in Week 4. Sit Henry. Buffalo has allowed the seventh-fewest yards per target and the fourth-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to tight ends.

After starting this season with a 72.1% route share in Week 1, Pat Freiermuth has seen route shares of 56.5% and 56.8% over the last two games. This isn't ideal. Freiermuth was a popular streaming option at tight end that I also liked last week, but he faceplanted. Since Week 2, he has had only a 12.2% target share with 1.32 YPRR, zero red zone targets, two deep targets, and a 12.8% first-read share. He's a sit this week against a defense that ranks 16th in yards per target allowed to tight ends while giving up the 13th-fewest fantasy points per opportunity to the position.

I don't know why Atlanta gave Kyle Pitts a contract extension to not use him as a focal point in the offense. It makes no sense, but this is what we're seeing. Pitts has a 53.7% snap rate, a 58.9% route share, only a 7.6% target share with 0.38 YPRR, zero red zone targets, one deep target, and an 8.3% first-read share. Last week, with Michael Penix, Kyle Pitts had an 8% target share, five receiving yards, and a 5% first-read share. Until his usage trends upward, he's a weekly sit.

AJ Barner is a viable low-end streaming option at tight end this week. Barner has a 12.5% target share, 1.32 YPRR, four red zone targets, and a 12.9% first-read share. He's a touchdown-or-bust streaming option. Last week, he was the TE14 in fantasy while seeing a 19.6% target share with 69 receiving yards (2.09 YPRR) and a 22.6% first-read share. The Bolts have allowed the 13th-most yards per target to tight ends.

Last week, Oronde Gadsden goose-egged. He had an 8.8% target share with a 65.8% route share, but he finished with zero receptions and a 4.8% first-read share. Hopefully, better days are ahead for him, but I'm not starting Gadsden in any league this week. Seattle has allowed the third-fewest yards per target to tight ends.

In his first game back in an Eagles' jersey, Zach Ertz had a 38.3% snap rate, a 35.5% route share, a 7.7% target share, and an 11.8% first-read share. These are all encouraging numbers out of the gate for Ertz, but the usage isn't enough at this point to put him on the fantasy radar. I expect his snap share to rise this week, but until that happens, he isn't in the streaming spectrum.

Terrance Ferguson opened the week with a DNP (ankle). He sustained an ankle injury last week. I don't expect him to play this week, but I'll update his outlook on Friday. I'll likely be adding Tyler Higbee to the Primer on Friday.
Mason Taylor is week-to-week with a thumb injury. I'm expecting him to sit again this week. He opened this week with a DNP.

Will Anderson was excellent in Week 3, racking up five solos, two assists, 2.5 sacks, three tackles for loss, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery. Anderson is up to four sacks on the season and has cemented himself as one of the early favorites for Defensive Player of the Year. Tap Anderson as a top-five option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Jeffery Simmons went off in Week 3, tallying five solos, five assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. The sack makes it two straight games with a QB takedown for the mega-talented defensive tackle. Tap Simmons as an easy top-20 option going forward.

Greg Rousseau stayed hot in Week 3, racking up five solos, three assists, two sacks, and four tackles for loss on 81 percent of the snaps. Rousseau has been a man on a mission to start the season, recording two sacks every game this season, to put him at 6.0 through three contests. The Bills edge rusher will look to stay hot in Week 4 against a struggling New England Patriots offense. Tap Rousseau as a top-10 play for the plus matchup.

Danielle Hunter was solid in Week 3, generating two solos, four assists, 0.5 sacks, one forced fumble, and one pass defended. Hunter is up to 1.5 sacks on the season and should really start to get going now that Will Anderson is seen as the superior threat by most opposing offensive coordinators. The sacks will still likely come in bunches, but should start adding up as soon as this week against the Dallas Cowboys.

Tuli Tuipulotu showed up in Week 3, reeling off five solos, one assist, 1.5 sacks, and one tackle for loss. The sack was the first of the season for Tuli, who is getting used to playing more of a full time role for the Chargers' defensive front. He has actually been showing up in the run game, so this could be a permanent ascension, even once Akheem Mesidor is ready for a more full complement of snaps. Tuli's slow start has dropped him down to the DL2 conversation, but he becomes one of the elites in that range. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Seattle Seahawks.

DeForest Buckner was back at it in Week 3, racking up two solos, five assists, 1.5 sacks, and one tackle for loss. Buckner is up to three sacks on the season, with at least a half sack in each game, and a full sack in two straight. Buckner has always been one of the higher floor DT options due to his weekly tackle upside, pushing him into the DL2 conversation during some lean bye weeks. However, now that he appears to be in vintage form as he plays for a new contract, he should be a weekly top-25 conversation as long as he is cooking. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against Washington on Sunday morning.

Leonard Williams has been on fire to start the season, racking up two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss. Williams has registered a sack in every game so far this season, for a total of three. Treat him as a DL2 option as long as he is cooking.

Chase Young showed up again in Week 3, tallying two solos, two sacks, two tackles for loss, and one forced fumble on 76 percent of the snaps. Young is now up to an impressive 3.5 sacks on the season, with a full sack in each of his last two. Young is a DL2 option given the right matchup and should be treated as one regardless of matchup as long as he is cooking. He may settle in as more of a DL3 when the sacks become more sporadic. Tap the talented edge rusher as a top-25 option for Week 4, thanks to a plus matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on Monday Night Football.

Mason Graham has arrived. Graham was at it again in Week 3, showing out with four solos, three assists, two sacks, and three tackles for loss on 68 percent of the snaps. The Browns' interior pass rusher now has a sack in each of his first three games and is up to four on the season. Graham has transformed from run stuffer to pass rushing disruptor and should only continue to add to his ledger. Count him as a DT1/DL3 option everywhere for Thursday Night Football against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Dexter Lawrence was excellent in Week 3, racking up three solos, one assist, two sacks, and three tackles for loss on 77 percent of the snaps. The sacks were the first of the season for the talented defensive tackle, who should continue to be counted as a DT1 option who also offers DL3 value, especially during the byes.

Isaiah McGuire showed up in Week 3, notching two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 63 percent of the snaps. McGuire saw an expanded role with Alex Wright lost for the season and should continue to as long as he performs well. The sack was the first of the season for the Browns edge rusher. McGuire is now a DL3/4 option and should be treated as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers.

Sheldon Rankins showed up again in Week 3, tallying three solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 71 percent of the snaps. Rankins has recorded a sack in two straight games to put him at two for the season. His play has put him squarely in the DT2 mix going forward, and he could provide matchup-based DT1 upside during the byes.

Princely Umanmielen showed up again in Week 3, racking up two solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 37 percent of the snaps. Princely has a sack in two of his three games, putting him at two for the season. He has seen his role expand since recording a sack in Week 1, but is likely to stay in a strict rotational role against the Lions in Week 4. He has made himself worth a roster spot in deeper leagues, but 40 percent of the snaps makes him too risky to plug into lineups outside of 32 team leagues. Look elsewhere for Week 4.

Derick Hall showed up in Week 3, racking up two solos, two assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss on 51 percent of the snaps. Hall now has two sacks in three games despite playing a rotational role for Mike McDonald's defense. His snap share is going to keep his tackle count lower than one would like most weeks, but there is no arguing with his production through three weeks of the season. Tap Hall as a DL3 option as long as he is cooking, including this week, thanks to a plus matchup against a struggling Los Angeles Chargers offense.

DJ Wonnum showed up in a big way in Week 3, recording two solos, two sacks, and two tackles for loss on 66 percent of the snaps. Wonnum has seen his role fluctuate for the Lions but should have earned himself a more prominent snap share after his Week 3 success. The Lions edge rusher makes for a solid depth piece for the byes, but is not someone you should be starting in Week 4 with no teams on bye. Look elsewhere for Week 4, despite the plus matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

Malcolm Koonce showed up again in Week 3, registering three solos, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble on 47 percent of the snaps. Koonce now has a sack in two straight games, putting him at 2.5 sacks on the season. Koonce is producing despite being a rotational piece behind workhorse Maxx Crosby and Kwity Paye, who sees close to 60 percent of the snaps. Koonce is worth a deep league DL3/4 look where needed while he is cooking. Treat him as such for Week 4 against Kansas City.

DaVon Hamilton showed out in Week 3, tallying three solos, two assists, 0.5 sacks, one forced fumble, and one fumble recovery on 51 percent of the snaps. DaVon offers value in DT leagues but does not play enough snaps to be starter worthy in DL leagues. Feel free to stash him in 20+ team leagues, but those in 12 team DL leagues should look elsewhere altogether. Wait to see more from Hamilton before even considering rostering him.

Akheem Mesidor was excellent in Week 3, tallying two solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Mesidor is playing behind Khalil Mack and Tuli Tuipulotu but is continuing to push for an expanded role. With that said, he was drafted to be a rotational piece in his rookie season, so he will likely stay third in snaps, barring an injury ahead of him, especially with Tuli improving in the run game. Treat Mesidor as a DL4 with DL3 upside during the byes.

Keldric Faulk showed up in Week 3, tallying three solos, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 59 percent of the snaps. The sack was the first of the season for Faulk, who has ample runway to continue to add to his sack ledger in the coming weeks. For now, treat him as more DL4 than DL3, with an eye on him becoming more than just solid bye week filler in the coming weeks.

Khristian Boyd showed up in Week 3, registering two solos, one assist, one sack, and two tackles for loss on 34 percent of the snaps. The sack was the first of the season for Boyd, who could develop into an IDP option down the line but is not yet playing enough snaps to be an option. Stash him in 20+ team leagues if so desired.

Roquan Smith was excellent in Week 3, tallying three solos, six assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Roquan is in the LB1 overall discussion for Week 4, thanks to a tasty matchup against Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans. Start him everywhere for what could be another spike week.

Blake Cashman was at it again in Week 3, tallying three solos, five assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Cashman has a sack in two straight games as an off-ball linebacker and is up to 2.5 on the season. The LB5 through three weeks of action, it's time to start taking Cashman seriously as a top-12 option again. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Jacob Rodriguez was excellent in Week 3, reeling off four solos, two assists, three tackles for loss, one interception, and one pass defended. Rodriguez has had a strong start to his rookie season, pushing his way into the LB2 conversation after just three weeks of action. Count him as a top-25 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

Nick Bolton was at it again in Week 3, tallying eight solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Bolton has recorded six or more solos in two straight games and has made his case to stay in the LB1 conversation despite the emergence of new names in that discourse. The LB13 through three weeks of action, start Bolton everywhere as a top-10 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders.

Kaden Elliss showed up in Week 3, recording four solos, five assists, and one tackle for loss. Elliss is playing an everydown role for New Orleans but has managed just an LB2-level output through three weeks of action, disappointing some fantasy managers. The production has been solid and the spike weeks are sure to continue. Treat Elliss as a top-30 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons.

Tremaine Edmunds showed up in Week 3, racking up six solos, four assists, and one pass defended. Edmunds had zero solos in a nondescript Week 2 outing against Los Angeles, but has at least six solos in his other two games this season. His role and production put him in the top-25 mix, but Arvell Reese is improving week by week and may start to soak up more of the tackle and pass rushing opportunities. Count Edmunds as a strong LB2 play for Week 4, thanks to a plus Week 4 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

Eric Wilson showed up in Week 3, racking up six solos, four assists, 1.5 sacks, two tackles for loss, and one pass defended on 99 percent of the snaps. Wilson had a quiet start to the season that led to panic by some IDP managers, putting Wilson back in the mix on the waiver wire. Wilson may not be the LB2 mainstay that he was in past seasons, but he still makes for a high upside LB3 play due to his snap alignment in Brian Flores' scheme. He lines up on the line of scrimmage and is presented with rush opportunities enough that his spike weeks can help you win your fantasy matchup. Tap Wilson as a top-25 option for Week 4, thanks to a tasty matchup against the tanking Miami Dolphins.

Demario Davis showed up in Week 3, notching seven solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Demario is an everydown player for the Jets, putting him in the LB3 mix. He is not the most exciting option, but he will have his spike weeks and makes for an excellent LB4 play who can slot in during the byes. Tap Davis as a borderline top-36 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Chicago Bears.

Drake Thomas continued his strong play in Week 3, generating five solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. The LB12 through three weeks of action, Thomas will likely be ineligible for this column going forward. He has been a locked-in LB2 play since last season, and we have been some of his biggest fans. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the struggling Los Angeles Chargers.

Jack Gibbens showed up in Week 3, reeling off four solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss on 96 percent of the snaps. Gibbens is playing nearly every snap for Arizona after winning the starting job over Cody Simon this summer and seems to be in zero danger of Simon stealing snaps any time soon. Gibbens is a solid LB3 candidate for Week 4, thanks to a plus matchup against the banged-up New York Giants.

Arvell Reese flashed his upside in Week 3, racking up 10 solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Reese has recorded five or more solos in two of his three contests so far and should be counted as a top-20 option going forward. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Arizona Cardinals.

Patrick Queen showed up in Week 3, racking up four solos, nine assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Queen is manning the everydown role for the Steelers, but this was his first outing with more than two solos. He remains an LB3 option due to his role and upside, but it appears that inconsistency will be a constant again this season. Tap Queen as a top-36 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Cleveland Browns.

Sonny Styles was excellent in Week 3, racking up four solos, one assist, one forced fumble, one interception, and one pass defended. The LB28 through three weeks of action, Styles should settle in as an upside LB2 option as the season progresses and is well worth being viewed as such. Tap him as a top-25 option for what should be a busy afternoon against Jonathan Taylor and the Indianapolis Colts offense.

Daiyan Henley was excellent in Week 3, racking up five solos, four assists, one forced fumble and two fumble recoveries. Henley has had a slow start to the season, with this being his first game with more than two solos. The muted production has dropped him to the LB3 ranks, but his performance against Buffalo reminds us of his upside. For now, continue to treat him as a top-36 option.

Derrick Barnes was at it again in Week 3, tallying five solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Barnes has forced his way into the top-15 discussion with his LB1-level play through the first three weeks of the season and currently sits as the LB7 in total fantasy points. Star Barnes everywhere as a top-15 option going forward.

T.J. Edwards finally showed up in Week 3, recording two solos, one assist, one tackle for loss, one interception, and three passes defended. Edwards was excellent in Week 3 due to his activity against the pass, including the late game pick, but has still managed just two or fewer solos in every game so far this year. He does have a potential 'get right' matchup on tap in Week 4 against the New York Jets, but with no byes, he presents more risk than is necessary due to his new bench floor. Look elsewhere for your Week 4 LB3.

Quincy Williams showed up in Week 3, tallying five solos, four assists, and one tackle for loss. Quincy has had a solid start to the season and can be counted as a borderline LB2/LB3 play. Fire him up as a top-30 option for what should be a productive Thursday Night Football game for the Browns linebacker.

Alex Anzalone showed up in Week 3, racking up two solos, three assists, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Anzalone has managed just two solos in each of his games this season, dropping him to LB4/5 territory despite his everydown role. He should produce more in line with what we have seen from him in the past when he gets more comfortable in the scheme, but an assist-heavy fantasy line does not help anyone outside of the byes. Keep Anzalone benched for Week 4, with an eye on having him fill in during the byes.

Trenton Simpson was back at it again in Week 3, notching five solos, two assists, two tackles for loss, and one fumble recovery. Simpson has done everything he could to make a case to stay ahead of Teddye Buchanan once both are healthy, and we will need to see how it plays out. Teddye played just four percent of the snaps in his first week back, and Head Coach Jesse Minter has been impressed enough that Simpson will likely get at least one more week of starting duties ahead of Buchanan. The more likely scenario is that Simpson will have to become a liability again before the team goes to Teddye. Add and start Simpson everywhere as an LB3 option ahead of a tasty Week 4 matchup against the Tennessee Titans.

Jaishawn Barham stayed hot in Week 3, racking up four solos, three assists, and two tackles for loss on 56 percent of the snaps. Barham has performed beyond expectations filling in for the injured DeMarvion Overshown and has likely earned himself a similar role, even when DeMarvion returns. Dee Winters may actually be the one who has to share some of his snaps. Whatever the case, Barham is an LB3 option while he is producing and should be treated as one for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Houston Texans.

Omar Speights showed up in Week 3, notching three solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble on 60 percent of the snaps. Speights played a season high in snaps against Denver and could see another 60 percent workload against Philadelphia due to the presence of Saquon Barkley and Jalen Hurts. With that said, Speights has just the three solos on the season and played just 34 and 52 percent of the snaps in the prior two weeks. With muted production and a fluctuating role, Speights should be left on fantasy benches, at least for one more week until the byes start forcing hands. Keep him rostered, but look elsewhere for your Week 4 LB3/4.

Khalil Mack showed up in Week 3, racking up two solos, two assists, one sack, and two tackles for loss. The sack makes it two straight games getting to the quarterback for the veteran, who is now up to two sacks on the season. Mack has played roughly 70 percent of the snaps through three weeks of the season, but with Akheem Mesidor finding his footing, it will likely not be long before Mack starts seeing his snaps scaled back. For now, count Khalil as a DL3 with matchup-based DL2 upside.

Kain Medrano was excellent in Week 3, reeling off three solos, two assists, one interception, one pass defended, and one touchdown on 66 percent of the snaps. Medrano sealed the game with his pick-six off Sam Darnold and may be tasked with a rotational role for the rest of the year now that Leo Chenal (neck) has been confirmed to be out for the season. Medrano is more of a deep league speculative add for now, as there is a high chance that the Commanders kick the tires on trade or free agent depth. Kain was a special teams player only before his breakout, so Washington may not be ready to hand him 50 percent or more of the snaps for the next 14 weeks of the season.

Kyle Van Noy showed up in Week 3, racking up three solos, two assists, 1.5 sacks, and three tackles for loss on 25 percent of the snaps. Van Noy hasn't seen more than 40 percent of the snaps this season, but is going to be able to make an impact in a situational role, as we have seen in previous stops. That will not translate much for fantasy purposes, as his production will be true boom-or-bust, sporadic, and inconsistent based on his weekly role, but in real life he can help keep Dallas Turner and Andrew Van Ginkel fresh while also providing an extra pass rushing option when all three are on the field. The sack was the first of the season for Van Noy, and barring an injury ahead of him, the veteran should be left on benches for Week 4 and beyond. Look elsewhere for your Week 4 DL3.

Kyle Hamilton was rock solid in Week 3, tallying four solos, four assists, one tackle for loss, and two passes defended. The DB8 through three weeks of action, Hamilton is one of only four players linked to the top-12 in draft rooms who has been a DB1 so far. Tap Hamilton as a top-five option for a tasty Week 4 matchup against Cam Ward and the Tennessee Titans.

Dillon Thieneman impressed in Week 3, racking up four solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. The rookie safety is settling in as a DB2 option; he has 15 solos on the season, and the best has yet to come. Count Thieneman as an upside top-25 play for Week 4, thanks to a plus matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Jordan Battle showed up in Week 3, racking up three solos, one assist, one interception, and one pass defended. Battle offers solid DB2 value, but is unlikely to crack the DB1 code unless he can show some more consistency and upside in the solo department. Tap him as a top-20 option for Week 4.

Jeremy Chinn was excellent in Week 3, racking up seven solos, one assist, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. The DB5 through three weeks of action, Chinn is locked in the top-10 conversation and should be treated as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Talanoa Hufanga went off in Week 3, exploding for two solos, three assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, two interceptions, three passes defended, and one touchdown. The AFC Defensive Player of the Week has been locked in as a DB1 option through three weeks of action, with the massive spike week pushing him up to DB1 overall in fantasy points. Continue to treat Hufanga as a top-1
0 option for Week 4.

Xavier Watts showed up in Week 3, tallying two solos, three assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Watts has produced like more of a borderline DB2 than the elite DB2 many expected him to be, but maintains his top-15 weekly upside. Tap him as a top-25 option for Monday Night Football against the New Orleans Saints.

Brandon Jones exploded for 10 solos, two assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended for the Denver Broncos in Week 3. Jones saw more snaps in the box due to facing off against the Los Angeles Rams and their 12 and 13 personnel heavy offense, and responded with what will likely be his season high in solo tackles. Jones is a strong DB3 option for Week 4 and beyond and should be rostered in all competitive leagues. Treat him as such for what should be another busy afternoon against the San Francisco 49ers in Week 4.

Joshua Metellus showed up in Week 3, tallying four solos, five assists, 0.5 sacks, and one pass defended. Metellus has just 11 solos on the season, but has managed four solos in two straight. He remains a DB3 option, but is teetering on the DB4 periphery. Tap him as a top-36 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Miami Dolphins.

Xavier McKinney showed up in Week 3, racking up four solos, one assist, one interception, and one pass defended. Xavier has slipped to the DB3 realm due to his slow start, but his Week 3 production swings his fantasy arrow back in the right direction. Treat McKinney as a top-36 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the banged-up Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

Kamari Lassiter showed up in Week 3, tallying six solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Lassiter is locked in as an upside-based DB3 option who doubles as a CB1 in CB leagues. He is a proven IDP asset, playing opposite Derek Stingley, and should see plenty of work this weekend against the Dallas Cowboys. Tap Lassiter as a top-30 option, thanks to the plus matchup.

Alontae Taylor stepped up in Week 3, racking up four solos, one sack, and one tackle for loss. Taylor has recorded four or more solos in two straight games and remains locked in as a CB1/DB3 option. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Chuck Clark was excellent in Week 3, racking up three solos, four assists, one sack, one tackle for loss, and one forced fumble. Clark offers solid DB3 value as a starter for the Lions, a role he should have at least until the Lions return from bye in Week 7. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Carolina Panthers.

CJGJ showed up in Week 3 for the Buffalo Bills, notching three solos, two assists, one interception, and two passes defended.  Gardner-Johnson remains a top-25 option, but has lost some of his IDP upside due to playing more of his snaps deep in the Bills' defensive scheme. He is still more than worthy of a DB2 or even a DB3 play, but we can no longer expect him to push for DB1 numbers over the course of a full season sans at least a handful of interceptions. Tap CJGJ as a top-25 option for a suddenly tasty Week 4 matchup against the New England Patriots.

Reed Blankenship showed up in Week 3, tallying five solos, four assists, one interception, and two passes defended.  Blankenship has been a solid DB3 option to open the season, but flashed some of his DB2 upside against Indianapolis. For now, continue to treat him as a DB3 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.

Andre Cisco was at it again in Week 3, tallying five solos, one assist, one sack, and one tackle for loss. He has recorded at least four solos in every game this season and made for a strong DB3 option with what turned out to be DB2 upside. However, Minkah Fitzpatrick was able to log a limited practice session on a Wednesday, suggesting that he may be able to suit up for Week 4, which in turn would send Cisco back to the bench. It was a good run for Cisco, but he is likely to see minimal (if any) snaps once Minkah is healthy. Prepare contingency plans for Week 4.

Christian Izien stepped up in Week 3, reeling off nine solos, two assists, three tackles for loss, and one pass defended on 97 percent of the snaps. Izien played just 36 percent of the snaps in Week 2, but played nearly every snap in Week 3 with Brian Branch and Kerby Joseph still sidelined. Izien should have at least one more start for IDP managers who find themselves in a bind and makes for an intriguing low-end DB3.

Hezekiah Masses was at it again in Week 3, reeling off four solos, two assists, one interception, and one pass defended. Masses now has a highly impressive three interceptions in two weeks filling in for the injured Darien Porter (foot), and may not be ready to give the starting role back. Masses has recorded four solos in two straight games, proving to be a worthy CB2/DB4 candidate if he continues to get starts. He is more of a deep league and speculative add, but Masses has shown enough to be worth a roster spot in leagues with deep benches.

Ronnie Hickman was excellent in Week 3, reeling off three solos, five assists, one interception, and one pass defended.  Hickman has recorded a sack or a pick in two straight games, ensuring that Emmanuel McNeil-Warren stays bolted to the bench outside of three safety looks. Hickman should have bought himself plenty of runway with his strong play to start the season. Add that to the Browns' surprsing early season success, and EMW may have to wait until late in the season, or even 2027, before he ascends to the starting lineup. This means Hickman projects as a safe DB3 option with no threat of losing his job during the byes. Tap him as a top-36 option for Thursday Night Football.

Dru Phillips was excellent in Week 3, racking up eight solos and three assists. Dru is a proven CB2 commodity who can double as a DB3 option in 20+ team leagues. However, for those of us in 12 team DB leagues, Phillips is not yet much of a fantasy option outside of a spot start in a heavy bye. He does play in the slot, which is why he offers some value outside of 32 team leagues, but will need to show more consistency to be viewed as a reliable DB3 option. Look elsewhere for Week 4.

Mansoor Delane showed up in Week 3, registering seven solos, three assists, one tackle for loss, and one pass defended. Mansoor played an every snap role for the Chiefs and should offer strong CB2 value for IDP managers. He has not yet entered the DB3 conversation but could join the discussion during the byes,

Marcus Harris stayed hot in Week 3, reeling off five solos, two assists, and two tackles for loss. Harris has been shining in his slot role, recording at least four solos and two assists in every game this season. His consistency has locked him into the DB3 conversation during the byes and has propelled him to elite CB1 territory. At this point, Harris is one of the few corners who deserve to be plugged into lineups, even outside of the byes. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Baltimore Ravens.

Amik Robertson stepped up in Week 3, tallying four solos, two assists, one forced fumble, and four passes defended. Amik has recorded four or more solos in two straight games, putting him in the CB2/DB4 mix. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Indianapolis Colts. If you need a DB3, however, look elsewhere, at least until the byes.

Renardo Green solidified himself as a CB2 option with his second strong game in three weeks, recording seven solos, six assists, and one pass defended. Green registered just three combined solos in his prior two games but had a pick in Week 1, which is what helps keep him on the CB2 radar as opposed to just being someone to add to watch lists. Roster him in CB leagues, but keep him on benches unless you need a CB3.

C.J. Henderson showed out in Week 3, reeling off eight solos and three passes defended. Henderson is being handed an expanded role with A.J. Terrell landing on I.R.and responded with an impact performance while leading the cornerback group in snaps. Henderson becomes an immediate CB2 option and could work his way into the CB1/DB1 co
nversation during the byes.

Quinyon Mitchell was at it again in Week 3, tallying six solos, one assist, two tackles for loss, and two passes defended. Mitchell is a top-12 CB option due to his upside and production and could be a solid DB3 option during the byes. For now, treat him as a CB1/DB4 option for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Los Angeles Rams.

Taron Johnson was a busy man on Sunday, racking up seven solos, one assist, one fumble recovery, and one pass defended against the New Orleans Saints. Johnson is playing in the slot for Las Vegas, so he could settle in as a DB3 option eventually. For now, he is more of a CB league play, where he can be counted as a borderline CB1 option. Treat him as such for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs.

Genesis Smith made a name for himself on Sunday, breaking out with two solos, three assists, two interceptions, and two passes defended on 63 percent of the snaps. Smith has seen his snap share grow each week and has likely earned the full confidence of the coaching staff. Derwin James, of course, has the more valuable role of the starting safety duo, but Smith has proven he can be an IDP option despite playing the bulk of his snaps deep.

Calen Bullock was at it again in Week 3, racking up five solos, three assists, and one tackle for loss. Bullock has recorded five solos in both of his games this season, keeping him locked in as a DB2 option. Treat him as a top-25 play for a plus Week 4 matchup against the Dallas Cowboys.
